meta.title: Travellers Rest (Judge John Overton House), Nashville: measured record for the 3D model
read_this_first: HABS TN-14 contains NO measured-drawing sheets: only 11 photographs, 10 data pages and a caption page. The plan (p. 8) and south elevation (p. 9) are small tracings by Patrick W. Crawford (NPS, 1970) from the restoration architects' drawings, with a graphic scale bar and no written dimensions.

Every length below is therefore scaled from a scale bar on a 200 dpi scan (plan 1 px = 28 mm, elevation 1 px = 14 mm) or derived from a photograph or an aerial image. Nothing here is a dimension string. Tolerances are stated per value.

The dimensioned originals exist but are not online: Warterfield and Bass, 'Architectural Restoration of John Overton's Home', Project 6605, June 1966, 17 sheets; Brush, Hutchison & Gwinn, 'Restoration of 1828 Addition', 29 May 1969; HABS field records FN-24 at the Library of Congress (unprocessed).
meta.units: feet as scaled from the drawings and metres

frame.description: The model frame of docs/WORLD_ENGINE.md: metres, Y up, +Z = nominal south (the front), -X = nominal west. x = 0 on the south-door axis, z = 0 at mid-depth of the main block, y = 0 at exterior grade by the south door.
frame.plan_pixel_to_model: x_m = -(px - 824.5) * 0.027609 ; z_m = (706.75 - py) * 0.027609 on the native 1650 x 2181 scan of PDF page 9 (printed p. 8)
frame.nominal_vs_true: HABS calls the front 'south'. The front actually faces true azimuth 238 degrees (see orientation). 'South', 'west' and so on in this file are the survey's nominal directions unless marked true.

elevation.reading: bar ticks at native x = 238 (15 ft), 347, 457, 568 (0), 680 (-5 ft)

scale_bars.cross_check: Plan overall 52.1 x 106.1 ft against the HABS text 'approximately 52 x 107 ft' (within 1 %). The elevation makes the front 51.3 ft, 1.5 % short of the plan: horizontal positions on the elevation carry +/- 2 %.

confidence_scale.high: two independent sources agree, or a label/caption states it
confidence_scale.medium: scaled from one scale bar, or counted on a clear photograph
confidence_scale.low: inferred, or read on aerial imagery to a metre or worse

which_room_is_the_library.value: The WEST room of the main block (the southwest room), west of the entry hall.
evidence: It is lettered LIBRARY on the HABS plan, p. 8 (north arrow checked: the ell is on the north, the library on the west).
HABS photograph TN-14-8, 'First floor, southwest room, looking west', shows the same room: fireplace in the west wall, door to the ell in the north wall.
HABS text, p. 2: 'The mantel in the library was taken from a house in Franklin and installed in 1936.'

The 2021 photograph shows a vertical board seam between the second and third bays from the west: the two west bays are the 1812 addition. The library is therefore the room added in 1812 ('one room downstairs and one room above ... not joined by inside openings to the original four rooms', NRHP nomination 1969).
which_room_is_the_library.caveat: The name is the 1970 survey's. Whether Judge Overton used this room as his library was not established from a primary source in this pass.

conflicts.a: 1970 survey: pedimented portico with paired posts (built 1954)
conflicts.b: 2021 photograph: no portico, stone steps only
conflicts.follow: b, unless the model is declared to be the house as surveyed in 1970
conflicts.why: HABS itself dates the porch to 1954; it is neither Overton's nor present today.

conflicts.follow: plan for wall positions and overall size, elevation for heights and for opening sizes
conflicts.why: the plan agrees with the HABS text (52 x 107 ft) within 1 %; the elevation is drawn at twice the scale but is 1.5 % short across the front.

conflicts.a: plan: on the centre of the front
conflicts.follow: keep x = 0 on the door and take everything from it
conflicts.why: the difference is inside the tolerance of both drawings.

conflicts.a: plan 'reflects the building's appearance before the 1969 restoration'
conflicts.why: the 1969 work was to the brick ell; the Federal block had been restored in 1966. Do not use the plan for the ell's present interior.

conflicts.b: orthophoto: the front faces true azimuth 238 degrees (south-west by west)
conflicts.follow: b for sun and shadow; keep the nominal names for rooms and walls
conflicts.why: measured on georeferenced imagery and matched by OpenStreetMap.

grounds.state_recorded: as the site stands (orthophoto of early 2023, leaf-off), with what the 1970 survey and other texts add. No measured site plan was found; HABS TN-14 has none.
grounds.frame: offsets in metres from the south door threshold: x = nominal east (+) / west (-), z = nominal south (+, out from the front) / north (-). Add 3.12 to z to get the model's z. True north is toward (x -0.845, z -0.534).

outbuildings.name: law office (reconstruction of the 1950s)
outbuildings.description: one-storey brick, shingle roof, centre door between 9/9 windows, porch three-quarters of the front on four square posts (NRHP continuation sheet)
outbuildings.identified_by: HABS: 'brick law office on the south side'; NRHP: 'adjacent to the main front driveway'; the only small building there (OSM way 678286329)

cemetery.value: No family cemetery is shown or described on the present site in any source read. The house stands on a Mississippian village and burial ground (site 40DV11); Native graves lie under the grounds.
cemetery.source: museum pages on the first residents and on cultural resources; Tennessee Council for Professional Archaeology, 12 Sept 2022

lost_features: a semi-detached kitchen, probably a storey and a half, sought by excavation in 1988 under the 1820s and 1887 wings (museum 'Cultural Resources' page)
carriage house and more slave cabins built in the 1820s (HABS TN-14 data p. 1); positions unknown
ground-penetrating radar (New South Associates, about 2022) mapped 22 historic anomalies (drives, walks, walls, building foundations); the map itself was not obtained

terrain.value: the house stands on a rise ('the site's incline', TCLF); the elevation shows grade about 0.1 m higher at the door than at the corners. Metro Nashville publishes 2 ft contours (maps.nashville.gov Topographic/Contours) that were not read in this pass.

sources.repository: Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division
sources.shows: 11 photographs by Jack E. Boucher (5 exterior, 6 interior), 10 data pages, 1 caption page. NO measured-drawing sheets. Text gives overall size (approx. 52 x 107 ft), materials, window lights, stair type, outbuildings and the restoration history.
